ctx.text:
From a teenager in Bengaluru to the man who would dominate national headlines, Sukesh Chandrashekhar ’s story raises one extraordinary question: how did ONE man allegedly con his way into some of India’s most influential circles?
Netflix has announced Love Scam Aur Dhokha: The Sukesh Chandrashekhar Story, an upcoming true-crime documentary from India Today Originals. It delves into the extraordinary story of a man accused of orchestrating an elaborate web of deception.
The documentary comes from the makers of Curry & Cyanide: The Jolly Joseph Case and The Indrani Mukerjea Story: Buried Truth, two of Netflix India’s popular documentaries.
A story of multiple identities, audacious claims, alleged multi-crore fraud, and connections with glittering Bollywood stars and hushed acknowledgements in the corridors of powerful politicians, this is a saga that has gripped the nation, with twists that seem stranger than fiction.
Going beyond the headlines, the documentary draws on over two years of extensive research to trace Sukesh’s origin story that very few really know about. It also explores how he allegedly managed to operate on such a scale, even from inside Tihar jail, bringing to light the gaps in the system that allowed his operations to continue for so long.
Love Scam Aur Dhokha: The Sukesh Chandrashekhar Story explores the real story of not just what he’s accused of, but how the con kept working, and why people continued believing him.
The documentary is produced by India Today Originals, with Chandni Ahlawat Dabas serving as executive producer. It is directed by Moumita Sen and Niyantha Shekar, with Karan Rana as co-director. Munish Pandey and Shams Tahir Khan serve as crime consultants.
Love Scam Aur Dhokha: The Sukesh Chandrashekhar Story premieres on Netflix on December 18, 2026.
